notes: Data for `briefcase-ai connect`. Formats come from each tool's public documentation on verified_on. min_tested/max_tested are the tool versions the adapter was actually run against (null: never run against the real tool, documentation only). `supported` is a documentation-derived range; a detected version outside it falls back to print-only (override with --force). Entries under `unverified` are never written automatically. An `enforce` block describes the tool's blocking hook, used by `briefcase-ai policy` and `briefcase-ai hook <tool> --enforce`: the event, how a hook denies or asks, and what the tool does when the hook itself fails, each from the page in `docs_url` on `verified_on`.

claude-code.name: Claude Code
claude-code.tested: `claude mcp add/remove --scope user` and `claude plugin validate` on 2.1.330; telemetry export verified by the conformance harness on 2.1.330 (2026-11-21)

enforce.config: hooks.PreToolUse[] = {matcher, hooks: [{type: "command", command, timeout}]} in ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json or managed settings
enforce.matcher: tool name; a value with characters beyond letters, digits, _, -, space, comma and | is an unanchored JavaScript regular expression
enforce.input: JSON on stdin: session_id, cwd, permission_mode, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id; file tools send an absolute tool_input.file_path
enforce.deny: exit 0 with {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": "..."}}; exit code 2 with the reason on stderr also blocks
enforce.ask: the same object with permissionDecision "ask"; the reason is shown in the permission prompt
enforce.allow: printing nothing leaves the normal permission flow in place; permissionDecision "allow" would skip the permission prompt, so it is never sent
enforce.on_hook_failure: a hook that cannot start, exits with a code other than 0 or 2, prints invalid JSON or times out does not block the tool call; the handler field onFailure: "block" (Claude Code 2.1.295+) blocks instead
enforce.tested: Claude Code 2.1.330 run with `claude -p` against a local stub model API on 2026-11-22: the installed hook denied Bash and Read calls with the rule's reason, an ask became a denial in -p (nobody to answer), allowed calls ran, a broken policy failed open, fail_closed blocked, a missing launcher blocked with onFailure "block" and was allowed without it (fail-open command form), and `briefcase-ai policy off` removed the entry

enforce.trust: a new or changed non-managed hook is skipped until it is reviewed and trusted in /hooks

unverified: the apply_patch body grammar (file paths are read from `*** Add File:`, `*** Update File:`, `*** Delete File:` and `*** Move to:` lines)
permissionDecision "ask" is documented as unsupported, so an ask rule becomes the policy's ask_fallback
hosted tools such as WebSearch do not run PreToolUse, so web rules are not enforced in Codex
location of requirements.toml for managed hooks

events.preToolUse: allow | deny ("ask" is accepted by the schema but not enforced)

enforce.config: hooks.<event>[] = {command, timeout, matcher?, failClosed?} in ~/.cursor/hooks.json or .cursor/hooks.json; enterprise: /Library/Application Support/Cursor/hooks.json, /etc/cursor/hooks.json, C:\ProgramData\Cursor\hooks.json
enforce.input: JSON on stdin: conversation_id, hook_event_name, workspace_roots plus command and cwd (beforeShellExecution), tool_name, tool_input and mcp_server_name (beforeMCPExecution), file_path (beforeReadFile), tool_name and tool_input (preToolUse)
enforce.deny: exit 0 with {"permission": "deny", "user_message": "...", "agent_message": "..."}; exit code 2 also blocks
enforce.allow: {"permission": "allow"}; a permission hook that exits 0 with invalid or empty JSON blocks the action, so the hook always prints this
enforce.on_hook_failure: crashes, timeouts and exit codes other than 0 and 2 fail open; failClosed: true on the hook entry blocks instead
enforce.tested: never run against Cursor; the hook process is tested with payloads built from the documentation
unverified: tool_input field names for the Write and Delete tools in preToolUse (only the Shell example is documented); the hook reads file_path, path or target_file and allows the call when none is present
whether {"permission": "allow"} skips Cursor's own approval prompt for a command
no documented hook for web requests, so web rules are not enforced in Cursor
